journal_text: Never-Sold, of the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose, told me of Rows-For-Another, eleven years on an estate Owing of four months' work for a damaged boat. Never-Sold gave me the first price, 100 gold, mine to keep if words do the work. I'm to speak to Rows-For-Another on the channel bank, a short walk north of Blackrose along the swamp road.
directions: From the Chainbreakers' house take the swamp road north out of Blackrose; the channel bank is a short walk on, where the estate's steward stands with his book.

journal_text: Rows-For-Another will take the buy-out. By custom an Owing paid at its first price is closed, but Hulm-Tei, the estate's steward, holds her page, and its sum has grown every season. I'm to pay him the first price from Never-Sold's coin, or talk him into striking the page, on the channel bank beside her.
directions: Hulm-Tei stands a few steps from her on the bank.

journal_text: I talked Hulm-Tei, the estate's steward, round: Rows-For-Another has worked her four months many times over, and by custom that closes the Owing. He struck her page and gave it to me; Never-Sold's 100 gold is mine to keep. I'm to take the page to Never-Sold in the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose, back south down the swamp road.
directions: Back down the swamp road south into Blackrose.

journal_text: I paid Hulm-Tei, the estate's steward, the Owing's first price from Never-Sold's coin, and by custom that closes it. Hulm-Tei struck Rows-For-Another's page from the estate's book and gave it to me. I'm to take the page back south down the swamp road to Never-Sold in the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose.
directions: Back down the swamp road south into Blackrose.

journal_text: Rows-For-Another will not wait on a buy-out. She will go down the channel, out of the estate's reach, once Hulm-Tei, the estate's steward, has turned his back; she cannot drown in it, and she can never come back to the swamp road. I'm to go back south down the swamp road and tell Never-Sold in the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose.
directions: Back down the swamp road south into Blackrose.

journal_text: I gave Never-Sold, in the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose, Rows-For-Another's page, struck from the estate's book at the first price. By custom the Owing is closed and never mentioned again. Rows-For-Another may go home to her tree, and the boat stays with the estate.

I told Never-Sold, in the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose, that Rows-For-Another would not wait and was going down the channel. Never-Sold said the next one held will pay for it, but that she will not undo it. By now Rows-For-Another will have gone from the channel bank north of Blackrose, and she can never come back to the swamp road.
One of Never-Sold, Rows-For-Another and Hulm-Tei has died. Rows-For-Another's Owing can no longer be settled. The Chainbreakers have no more to ask of me in it.

Never-Sold told me that a fire went through Blackrose Prison, and the heirs keep three of their held at their stone house on Blackrose's east shore; one is Rows-For-Another's mother. She gave me 100 gold for Third-Born Tsaxi, their keeper, mine to keep if words do the work. I'm to talk Tsaxi round or pay him by the stone house.
directions: From the Chainbreakers' house go south-east through Blackrose to the shore; the stone house stands at the water's edge, and Tsaxi stands outside its west wall, on the town side.

journal_text: I talked Third-Born Tsaxi round: he will let one of the three go and tell the heirs the smoke took them. The heirs hold Says-It-Plain for his words, Hides-In-Reeds for a killing and Keeps-The-Old-Count, Rows-For-Another's mother, for her shelter; each stands by the stone house and will say why. I'm to tell Tsaxi which one goes.
directions: The three stand by the stone house, a few steps from Tsaxi; each will say why the heirs hold them.

journal_text: I paid Third-Born Tsaxi Never-Sold's 100 gold: he will let one of the three go and tell the heirs the smoke took them. The heirs hold Says-It-Plain for his words, Hides-In-Reeds for a killing and Keeps-The-Old-Count, Rows-For-Another's mother, for her shelter; each stands by the stone house and will say why. I'm to tell Tsaxi which one goes.
directions: The three stand by the stone house, a few steps from Tsaxi; each will say why the heirs hold them.

journal_text: I named Says-It-Plain to Third-Born Tsaxi at the heirs' stone house. Tsaxi will turn his back and Says-It-Plain will go, counted lost to the smoke; Hides-In-Reeds and Keeps-The-Old-Count stay held. I'm to go back north-west through Blackrose and tell Never-Sold in the Chainbreakers' house.
directions: Back north-west through Blackrose to the Chainbreakers' house.

journal_text: I named Hides-In-Reeds to Third-Born Tsaxi at the heirs' stone house. Tsaxi will turn his back and Hides-In-Reeds will go, counted lost to the smoke; Says-It-Plain and Keeps-The-Old-Count stay held. I'm to go back north-west through Blackrose and tell Never-Sold in the Chainbreakers' house.
directions: Back north-west through Blackrose to the Chainbreakers' house.

journal_text: I named Keeps-The-Old-Count, Rows-For-Another's mother, to Third-Born Tsaxi at the heirs' stone house. Tsaxi will turn his back and Keeps-The-Old-Count will go, counted lost to the smoke; Says-It-Plain and Hides-In-Reeds stay held. I'm to go back north-west through Blackrose and tell Never-Sold in the Chainbreakers' house.
directions: Back north-west through Blackrose to the Chainbreakers' house.

journal_text: I told Never-Sold, in the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose, that Third-Born Tsaxi let Says-It-Plain go from the heirs' stone house, counted lost to the smoke. Never-Sold said all three names back and keeps them. The heirs will take Hides-In-Reeds and Keeps-The-Old-Count back to the Rose once the fire's damage is mended.

I told Never-Sold, in the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose, that Third-Born Tsaxi let Hides-In-Reeds go from the heirs' stone house, counted lost to the smoke. Never-Sold said all three names back and keeps them. The heirs will take Says-It-Plain and Keeps-The-Old-Count back to the Rose once the fire's damage is mended.

I told Never-Sold, in the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose, that Third-Born Tsaxi let Keeps-The-Old-Count, Rows-For-Another's mother, go from the heirs' stone house, counted lost to the smoke. Never-Sold said all three names back and keeps them, and the heirs will take Says-It-Plain and Hides-In-Reeds back to the Rose once the fire's damage is mended. Never-Sold said she will see that what the heirs reckon the mother owes is never put on her daughter.

One of the three held at the heirs' stone house in Blackrose, Third-Born Tsaxi or Never-Sold has died. The heirs' count is short already. Those held cannot be let go now. The Chainbreakers have no more to ask of me in it.

Never-Sold, of the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose, told me of Ussa-Rekh, who bought out Owings for thirty years and now hires out the crews he freed at Soulrest. Heavy-Rope, the boss of one crew, sent word about him. I'm to find Heavy-Rope at the head of the dock at Soulrest, a short way east of Lilmoth along the coast.
directions: Soulrest's docks lie on the coast a short way east of Lilmoth; the map names them Soulrest. Heavy-Rope waits at the head of the dock.

journal_text: Heavy-Rope, the boss of a dock crew at Soulrest, told me his crew asked Ussa-Rekh to let them end their last season of hire early, and Ussa-Rekh refused. I'm to hear Ussa-Rekh's side; he stands just along the dock from Heavy-Rope.
directions: Ussa-Rekh stands a few steps from Heavy-Rope.

journal_text: Ussa-Rekh told me he freed these crews and they work the season as agreed: since the berths he bought began to cost more than their hire, a crew gone early leaves him unable to buy out the next. I'm to tell Heavy-Rope on the Soulrest dock whether I stand with his crew or with Ussa-Rekh.

I told Heavy-Rope I stand with his crew. Ussa-Rekh keeps their carved tokens until the last season is worked; a crew holding its own tokens owes him nothing more. Heavy-Rope gave me the crew's 50 gold, mine to keep if words get the tokens. I'm to talk Ussa-Rekh round or pay him for the tokens, just along the Soulrest dock.
directions: Ussa-Rekh stands a few steps from Heavy-Rope.

journal_text: I talked Ussa-Rekh round on the Soulrest docks, and he gave me the crew's carved tokens without the crew's coin. I'm to give the tokens to Heavy-Rope at the head of the dock.

I paid Ussa-Rekh on the Soulrest docks the crew's own coin for their last season, 50 gold, as if they had worked it, and he gave me their carved tokens. I'm to give the tokens to Heavy-Rope at the head of the dock.

I told Heavy-Rope at the head of the Soulrest dock that I stand with Ussa-Rekh and that his crew should take the refusal and work the season out. Heavy-Rope will not take it from a stranger without a reason worth hearing. I'm to talk him round, or pay 50 gold for his crew's lost days.
directions: Heavy-Rope waits at the head of the dock.

journal_text: On the Soulrest docks I stood with Heavy-Rope's crew against Ussa-Rekh, the broker who freed them and hires them still. I got their carved tokens from Ussa-Rekh and gave them to Heavy-Rope. A crew holding its own tokens owes Ussa-Rekh nothing more, and Heavy-Rope's crew will not work for him again.

On the Soulrest docks I stood with Ussa-Rekh, the broker who freed Heavy-Rope's crew and hires them still, and talked Heavy-Rope into taking his refusal. The crew will work their last season under Ussa-Rekh.

On the Soulrest docks I stood with Ussa-Rekh, the broker who freed Heavy-Rope's crew and hires them still, and paid Heavy-Rope 50 gold for his crew's lost days to take the refusal. The crew will work their last season under Ussa-Rekh.
Heavy-Rope or Ussa-Rekh is dead. The matter of the Soulrest crew's last season will never be settled now. I have no more to do in it.

I came to Claywater Station on the Blackwood Road. Travellers there pay Livia Varinius, the well-keeper, 2 drakes for the stop this season. Signs-For-The-Cargo, the landing's poler, now wants 1 drake from every walker who wades the ford. I'm to hear each keeper's side. Claywater Station is about 640 yards west of the signpost at Cartwright's Cross on the Blackwood Road, where the arms point to Gideon and to Leyawiin. Going west, a painted pole barrier stands in a field about 110 yards off the road on the right; that is the Drowning Gate. The station house roof comes into sight about 100 yards on, ahead on the left. Livia Varinius keeps the well at the station house door, inside the low stone walls. Signs-For-The-Cargo poles the plank raft at the landing stage across the ford, about 65 yards north of the well. The round mud huts stand behind it on the far bank. If the road runs on into open marsh with no roofs in sight, I have passed it.
directions: From the Blackwood Road: Claywater Station is about 640 yards west of the signpost at Cartwright's Cross, where the arms point to Gideon and to Leyawiin. Going west, a painted pole barrier stands in a field about 110 yards off the road on the right; that is the Drowning Gate, and the station house roof shows about 100 yards on, ahead on the left. The well stands at the station house door, inside the low stone walls. From the well, the raft and the landing stage are about 65 yards to the north, across the ford, with the round mud huts behind them on the far bank. If the road runs on into open marsh with no roofs in sight, you have passed it.

journal_text: At Claywater Station, Livia Varinius told me she raised the station's charge to 2 drakes to pay a mason to re-line the cracked well in stone. Signs-For-The-Cargo told me his people began charging walkers at the ford. The landing folk worked this ford before the well was dug. They will not haul stone for the station. Signs-For-The-Cargo says a crocodile has taken the landing's clay cut below the ford. The landing folk will hear terms only from whoever wins back the cut. I'm to kill the crocodile and bring back the clay basket that lies at the cut. The cut is below the ford on the station bank. From the well, I go about 45 yards west, outside the low stone walls, to where the river swings west under a bare clay bank and the water lies deep and dark. If the bank flattens into reeds, I have gone past it. Signs-For-The-Cargo says Takes-The-Short-Weight can tell what ails the station's water. She lives in the round mud hut on the landing bank, about 30 yards north of the raft.
directions: The clay cut is below the ford on the station bank: from the well, go about 45 yards west, outside the low stone walls, to where the river swings west under a bare clay bank and the water lies deep and dark. If the bank flattens into reeds, you have gone past it. Takes-The-Short-Weight lives in the round mud hut on the landing bank, about 30 yards north of the raft.

journal_text: I killed the crocodile at the clay cut below the ford at Claywater Station and showed Signs-For-The-Cargo the landing's clay basket. I'm to put terms to Livia Varinius and to Signs-For-The-Cargo: one charge of 2 drakes a stop, 1 to each bank, with the landing's clay rammed in behind the cracked lining. Livia Varinius says a mason's lining will mend the well and mud has no place in it. She says the landing folk would take half a charge for water they never draw. I'm to find out whether the well has cracked before. Takes-The-Short-Weight can taste the station's water if I bring it to her in Livia Varinius's dipper. Signs-For-The-Cargo says the station only wants stone. He will not haul it.
directions: Livia Varinius keeps the well inside the station walls; Signs-For-The-Cargo stands at the raft on the landing stage across the ford.

journal_text: I brought Livia Varinius and Signs-For-The-Cargo to terms at Claywater Station: one charge of 2 drakes a stop, 1 to each bank. The landing folk will ram their clay in behind the cracked lining. I killed the crocodile at the clay cut and gave the landing back its basket. Livia Varinius will send for no mason. Travellers no longer have a reason to wade below the cut.

I found that travellers at Claywater Station paid Livia Varinius at the well and again at the ford. I paid Signs-For-The-Cargo 100 drakes to take no charge from walkers this season, so they pay once, at the well. The well is still cracked.

I found that travellers at Claywater Station paid Livia Varinius at the well and again at the ford. I also found that the well's lining has cracked and been mended every year. To keep that quiet, Livia Varinius has dropped her charge back to the old drake. Signs-For-The-Cargo has dropped the walkers' charge in answer. Livia Varinius will send for no mason. The well is still cracked.

Livia Varinius is dead. The well at Claywater Station has no keeper now. The station's charge ended with her. Signs-For-The-Cargo keeps the landing's charge on the ford. The two charges cannot be settled now.
Signs-For-The-Cargo is dead. The raft at Claywater Station has no poler. The landing folk will make no terms with Livia Varinius while they mourn. Both charges stand.
Mee-Sei, who cooks at the fire stand in Greenspring, told me that guests at the lodge have been falling sick, and that people blame his food. I'm to find out what is making them ill.
directions: The pool lies under the Hist, a few steps from the fire stand; the lodge, where the sick guests lie, faces it across the spring.

journal_text: The guests at the Greenspring lodge sicken from the spring, not from Mee-Sei's food. Only Im-Moro, the spring-keeper, may go into the pool under the Hist. I'm to search the pool, with her leave or without it.
directions: The stone lip is on the lodge side of the pool; the Hist's roots go down into the water on the far side.

journal_text: I found a dead man staked in the throat of the spring at Greenspring and took the rope that tied his wrists. The stake through him is blank. That is what sickens the guests. I'm to find out who he was and who killed him.
directions: The lodge store is the locked room behind Haj-Tei's door; Reeh-Shaal keeps to the lodge.

journal_text: The courier who vanished from the Greenspring lodge twelve days ago lies in the spring, and what I have found points to Reeh-Shaal, the guest who says she waits for a boat to Helstrom. I'm to confront her with what I hold, and I need two things to make it stand.

I named Reeh-Shaal before the people of Greenspring as the one who killed the Helstrom courier and staked him in the spring. Im-Moro will raise the body and give it to the Hist, and Reeh-Shaal is to be held for Helstrom.
Reeh-Shaal is dead by my hand at Greenspring. Im-Moro will raise the courier's body from the spring, and the guests should mend.
I took the sealed packet from Reeh-Shaal at Greenspring and let her be. Nobody there will learn who killed the courier.
I accused Tsono-Ra of the courier's murder at Greenspring, and I was wrong. The villagers have closed ranks against me.

At Helstrom's landing, Okan-Zish of the landing crew told me a crocodile lairs in the shallows east of the scaffold. It took one of their rafts, and no raft has gone out since. I'm to kill it; it lies east of the rock roots where he stands, a short walk through the shallows.
directions: Okan-Zish stands on the rock roots at the landing. The crocodile lies in the shallows east of the scaffold, a short walk east of him.

journal_text: The crocodile in the shallows by the scaffold at Helstrom's landing is dead. I'm to tell Okan-Zish, the rafter of the landing crew who wanted it gone; he stands on the rock roots at the landing.
directions: Okan-Zish stands on the rock roots at the landing.

journal_text: Okan-Zish admitted the beast was the crew's doing: Wuleen-Taza dumped offal in the shallows east of the scaffold to scare traders off Sells-Dear's boat, and it drew a real crocodile. The crew left their bait bucket there. I'm to fetch it for Sells-Dear, the boat captain, which costs the crew their trade, or take Wuleen-Taza's price to keep quiet.
directions: The bucket lies in the shallows east of the scaffold. Wuleen-Taza stands east of Okan-Zish, near the bridge. Sells-Dear stands far north of the landing crew, on bare ground by the houses, with tents a short walk east of her.

journal_text: I have the crew's bait bucket, still sour with offal. I'm to show it to Sells-Dear, the boat captain, far north of the crew, on bare ground by the houses, and the crew lose their trade; or take Wuleen-Taza's price near the bridge and keep quiet.
directions: Sells-Dear stands far north of the landing crew, on bare ground by the houses; Wuleen-Taza east of Okan-Zish, near the bridge.

journal_text: I showed Sells-Dear, the boat captain, the crew's bait bucket. She kept it and paid me 60 gold, and with the rafters' trick known the river trade is hers. The landing crew have lost it: no trader hires their rafts now, and Okan-Zish and Wuleen-Taza have no work at the landing.

Wuleen-Taza paid me 60 gold to say nothing of the bait. The crew keep their trade, but I took coin to hide a trick that drew a real beast to the shallows by their scaffold, and Sells-Dear, the boat captain, still thinks the crocodile came up the river on its own.
Okan-Zish, a rafter of Helstrom's landing crew, is dead. What the crew asked of me ends with him.
Sells-Dear, the boat captain of Helstrom, is dead. What was asked of me at the landing ends with her.
Wuleen-Taza, a rafter of Helstrom's landing crew, is dead. What was asked of me at the landing ends with her.

Haj-Wan, who waits near Gih-Xaleel, the levy warden, by the paved road at Helstrom, told me her kin Sei-Wan walked out into the basin alone to prove himself to the Agaceph and has not come back. Their custom forbids his own to follow, but not an outsider. I'm to find him out among the trees, a long way east past the houses.
directions: East from the road, a long way past the houses; Sei-Wan is on dry ground among the trees there.

journal_text: I found Sei-Wan on dry ground out among the trees, a long way east of Helstrom's road. A viper lies south-west of him, a short walk off, and he will not come home while it lives. I'm to kill the viper.
directions: The viper lies among the trees south-west of Sei-Wan, a short walk off.

journal_text: The viper among the trees is dead, and Sei-Wan can walk home. Haj-Wan wants him home alive; he wants the walk-out to be his own. I'm to speak to him and choose: talk him home, which costs him the walk-out, or tell him to walk home alone and say nothing at the road.
directions: Sei-Wan is on dry ground a long way east of Haj-Wan, past the houses.

journal_text: Sei-Wan gave in and said he will come home, though not at my heels, and he will not count the walk-out as his own. Haj-Wan has waited for him since he left. I'm to tell her by the paved road, back west past the houses, near Gih-Xaleel, the levy warden.
directions: Haj-Wan waits by the paved road near the levy warden, back west past the houses.

journal_text: I told Sei-Wan to walk home on his own feet and left him on dry ground out in the basin, and I said nothing of it to Haj-Wan. His walk-out stays his own. Haj-Wan keeps waiting by the road and knows nothing.

I told Haj-Wan by the road that Sei-Wan is coming home, and she paid me 60 gold. She is glad he lives, and sorry that he lost the walk-out he went into the basin to win. I talked him out of it, and he will not thank me.
Sei-Wan, a young Agaceph of Helstrom, is dead in the basin. Whatever Haj-Wan asked of me for him ends with him, and the walk-out is lost to him for good.
Haj-Wan, who waited by Helstrom's road for her kin Sei-Wan, is dead. Whatever she wanted of me ends with her.

I woke in the hold of a ship, moored below Hereguard Plantation, west of Lilmoth in Black Marsh, among a gang of Argonians I do not know. I'm to go up the stairs and out of the door to the deck, and speak to the man who stands there.
directions: The hold's stairs climb to the one door, which opens onto the ship's deck; Buys-The-Months stands on the deck a few steps from the door.

journal_text: Buys-The-Months, the broker, died on the deck before he had said a word to me. The others on the deck have no help for a stranger. I'm to look for work in Lilmoth, east along the shore.
directions: East along the shore past the old lighthouse into Lilmoth; the marker leads to Salts-The-Catch's house, south of the second big ship anchored off Lilmoth's own dock.

journal_text: Buys-The-Months, the broker, holds his gang's Owing, the months of work they owe. I am on no line of his roll, so he will not keep me. He says Nesh-Deeka, a guest at Salts-The-Catch's house south of the second big ship off Lilmoth's dock, pays for work. I'm to find her there, east along the shore.
directions: From the ship, follow the shore east past the old lighthouse, into Lilmoth, as far as the second big ship, anchored off Lilmoth's own dock; Salts-The-Catch's house stands south of it, beside a wooden walkway, below the place the map calls Lilmoth Dock.

journal_text: A woman with a knotted cord killed Nesh-Deeka's courier at the gang's camp the night it burned, took his satchel and let me live. Nesh-Deeka serves the Veiled Reed, the state's quiet service, and wants a hand whose name is on no roll. I'm to hear her out and say whether I will work for the Reed.
directions: Nesh-Deeka is inside Salts-The-Catch's house.

journal_text: I took work with the Veiled Reed, and Nesh-Deeka put fifty gold in my hand. She has told me the first work the Reed wants of me. Why the woman with the knotted cord let me live, I still do not know.
Nesh-Deeka, who led the Veiled Reed's work in Lilmoth, is dead. The Reed has nothing more to ask of me.

Nesh-Deeka gave me the Veiled Reed's first work. Dives-Without-A-Rope, one of the broker's gang, carried off a jar of sap that the cutters dropped at the burnt camp. Nesh-Deeka wants it to learn what the cutters wanted. I'm to ask Dives-Without-A-Rope for the jar in the ship's hold at the pier west of Lilmoth.
directions: The broker's ship lies at the pier at Hereguard Plantation, west of Lilmoth, past the old lighthouse from the town; Dives-Without-A-Rope stands in its hold, and her lockbox sits at the far side of the hold with lockpicks beside it. Salts-The-Catch's house stands south of the second big ship, anchored off Lilmoth's own dock.

journal_text: Dives-Without-A-Rope is dead. Her lockbox is at the far side of the ship's hold, and the key is on her body. I'm to take the jar from the lockbox and bring it to Nesh-Deeka.
directions: The broker's ship lies at the pier at Hereguard Plantation, west of Lilmoth, past the old lighthouse from the town; Dives-Without-A-Rope stands in its hold, and her lockbox sits at the far side of the hold with lockpicks beside it. Salts-The-Catch's house stands south of the second big ship, anchored off Lilmoth's own dock.

journal_text: Dives-Without-A-Rope will not give up the jar. It is sap of her own tree, and she keeps it in her lockbox at the far side of the ship's hold, with the key on her. I'm to take the jar by picking the lock or by taking her key, and bring it to Nesh-Deeka.
directions: The broker's ship lies at the pier at Hereguard Plantation, west of Lilmoth, past the old lighthouse from the town; Dives-Without-A-Rope stands in its hold, and her lockbox sits at the far side of the hold with lockpicks beside it. Salts-The-Catch's house stands south of the second big ship, anchored off Lilmoth's own dock.

journal_text: I talked Dives-Without-A-Rope round. She gave me the key to her lockbox in the ship's hold. She asked me in return to find who cut her tree. I'm to take the jar from the lockbox and bring it to Nesh-Deeka.
directions: The broker's ship lies at the pier at Hereguard Plantation, west of Lilmoth, past the old lighthouse from the town; Dives-Without-A-Rope stands in its hold, and her lockbox sits at the far side of the hold with lockpicks beside it. Salts-The-Catch's house stands south of the second big ship, anchored off Lilmoth's own dock.

journal_text: I paid Dives-Without-A-Rope twenty gold. She gave me the key to her lockbox in the ship's hold. I'm to take the jar from the lockbox and bring it to Nesh-Deeka.
directions: The broker's ship lies at the pier at Hereguard Plantation, west of Lilmoth, past the old lighthouse from the town; Dives-Without-A-Rope stands in its hold, and her lockbox sits at the far side of the hold with lockpicks beside it. Salts-The-Catch's house stands south of the second big ship, anchored off Lilmoth's own dock.

journal_text: I tasted the cutters' sap in Salts-The-Catch's house. Nesh-Deeka wrote down what I said under it: a ship's hold with roots through its deck, a door that was never built, a dry voice. She gave me the page and twenty-five gold. She has heard that the Hist of Low-Reed Village, east of Lilmoth, has turned its face.
Nesh-Deeka is dead. I will not learn from her what the cutters wanted with the jar.

Nesh-Deeka told me the Hist of Low-Reed Village, a stilt village east of Lilmoth along the shore, has turned its face. She wants to know whether the cutters did this too. I'm to go there and speak to Hires-By-The-Season, the root-herald, who speaks for the village to strangers.
directions: Low-Reed Village stands on stilts over fresh water east of Lilmoth along the shore; Hires-By-The-Season stands on bare ground by the first house.

journal_text: Hires-By-The-Season, the root-herald, told me the Hist of Low-Reed Village shut eleven nights ago and the eggs in its pool died. The village blames the leeches and Pays-Late, the tree-minder, who will not say why he stands on the bank. I'm to get the truth out of him, on the bank under the stilts.
directions: Pays-Late stands on the bank under the stilts, on the village's south side, his gum box at his feet.

journal_text: Hires-By-The-Season, the root-herald of Low-Reed Village, is dead. Pays-Late, the tree-minder who keeps the village's Hist, stands on the bank under the stilts. I'm to ask him what happened to the tree.
directions: Pays-Late stands on the bank under the stilts, on the village's south side, his gum box at his feet.

journal_text: Pays-Late told me what he hid: the Hist's root was cut, its sap drawn off and the cut sealed with his own black gum. He kept quiet, fearing the villagers' blame. A boat came from the north reeds that night. I'm to cross the leech water to the giant tree's roots past the last stilt house and take the sap back.
directions: North of the village the reeds open onto the leech water; past it, beyond the last stilt house, a giant tree's roots rise out of the water in the reeds.

journal_text: I threatened to shame Pays-Late before the whole village, and he told me what he hid; he will not forget it. The Hist's root was cut, its sap drawn off and the cut sealed with his own black gum. I'm to cross the leech water to the giant tree's roots past the last stilt house and take the sap back.
directions: North of the village the reeds open onto the leech water; past it, beyond the last stilt house, a giant tree's roots rise out of the water in the reeds.

journal_text: I took the jars of Low-Reed Village's sap from two men at the giant tree's roots, jars like the one the cutters dropped at the burnt camp. Pays-Late can pour the sap back at the cut root, or Nesh-Deeka can keep it as proof. I'm to bring the jars to Pays-Late, on the bank under the stilts, and choose.
directions: Back south across the leech water to the village; Pays-Late stands on the bank under the stilts.

journal_text: I took the jars of Low-Reed Village's sap from two men at the giant tree's roots, jars like the one the cutters dropped at the burnt camp. Since I leaned on Pays-Late, he will not trust me to keep his secret. I'm to bring them to him and choose: back to his tree, or to Nesh-Deeka as proof.
directions: Back south across the leech water to the village; Pays-Late stands on the bank under the stilts.

journal_text: I told Pays-Late the jars go to the people I work for, as proof of the cutters' work, and kept them. Low-Reed Village's Hist stays dark while they are gone. I'm to bring them to Nesh-Deeka at Salts-The-Catch's house in Lilmoth, west along the shore.
directions: Lilmoth lies west along the shore; Salts-The-Catch's house stands south of the second big ship, anchored off Lilmoth's own dock.

journal_text: I gave the jars to Pays-Late and kept his secret. He will pour the sap back at the cut root, and Low-Reed Village will go on blaming him and the leeches. The cutters drew this tree's sap into jars, as they did at the burnt camp. What do they want with it?

I gave the jars to Pays-Late on one condition, that he tells Hires-By-The-Season himself that he found the cut and hid it, and he gave his word. He will pour the sap back at the cut root. The cutters drew this tree's sap into jars, as they did at the burnt camp. What do they want with it?

I gave the jars to Nesh-Deeka in Lilmoth, and she paid me fifty gold. She keeps them as proof of the cutters' work, so Low-Reed Village's Hist stays dark and the village still blames Pays-Late. The cutters drew that tree's sap into jars, as they did at the burnt camp. What do they want with it?
Pays-Late, the tree-minder of Low-Reed Village, is dead. The villagers will not tell a stranger what happened to his tree now.
Nesh-Deeka, the Veiled Reed's handler in Lilmoth, is dead. I cannot report to anyone what I learned at Low-Reed Village.
At Low-Reed Village I saw what the cutters do: a Hist cut at the root, its eggs dead and its sap drawn into jars. I'm to tell Nesh-Deeka at Salts-The-Catch's house in Lilmoth what I found.
directions: Salts-The-Catch's house stands south of the second big ship, anchored off Lilmoth's own dock.

journal_text: Nesh-Deeka told me a silent Hist kills no eggs but a cut one does, and the interior must learn the difference. Its tree-minders and Nisswo, the wandering priests who read the Hist, meet at Helstrom. I'm to go alone without naming the Reed and take the coast ship from Lilmoth's stop to Helstrom's river landing.
directions: The coast ship lies at Lilmoth's stop on the east side of the town; its door to Helstrom's landing is on the ship's upper deck, through the inner door.

journal_text: I came ashore at Helstrom's river landing. Among the trees by the stone towers west of the paved road, Ei-Tuja, a Nisswo, would preach my word in every village; Kaska-Meen, a tree-minder who hears few strangers, would carry it to the tree-minders alone. I'm to tell Ei-Tuja what I saw at Low-Reed Village, or ask him about Kaska-Meen.
directions: From the landing the way runs inland over roots and through shallows; partway along it, where it bends, the wasps keep the root. The way comes to a soldier on the paved road; the trees by the stone towers are west of it.

journal_text: Ei-Tuja says Kaska-Meen hears few strangers, and he will not speak for me. I'm to talk her round myself, among the trees by the stone towers, and tell her what I saw at Low-Reed Village.
directions: Kaska-Meen is among the trees by the stone towers, west of the paved road.

journal_text: What I saw at Low-Reed Village will not reach Kaska-Meen through me. Ei-Tuja, the Nisswo, hears anyone. I'm to tell him, among the trees by the stone towers.
directions: Ei-Tuja is among the trees by the stone towers, west of the paved road.

journal_text: I told Kaska-Meen what I saw at Low-Reed Village, and the tree-minders will hear it from her and shut their trees to strangers. She told me what a dying Hist leaves: a Mnemic Egg, a seed of its sap holding its memories, once used to stop a generation of eggs hatching. Is that what the cutters are gathering sap for?

I told Ei-Tuja what I saw at Low-Reed Village, and he will preach it openly in every village he walks to. He told me what a dying Hist leaves: a Mnemic Egg, a seed of its sap holding its memories, once used to stop a generation of eggs hatching. Is that what the cutters are gathering sap for?
Nesh-Deeka, the Veiled Reed's handler in Lilmoth, is dead. I cannot report to anyone what the Reed wanted said in Helstrom.
Ei-Tuja, the Nisswo who heard anyone and would have carried my word to the villages, is dead. What I saw at Low-Reed Village goes no further in Helstrom.

Root-Herald Ixo-Vaal of Greenspring asked me, for the Many-Root Conclave, to find out why the village's Hist is sickening. The villagers blame the salt works upstream. I'm to test the water before I believe them.
directions: The fork lies a short walk upstream of the river landing; the herald's house, with the salt sack at its door, faces the Hist.

journal_text: The salt in Greenspring's spring is not coming down the river. The couriers say the Hist's roots run into the flooded galleries of the Drowned Stair. I'm to go down and take water at each landing.
directions: From Greenspring take the road to the Gate-Side Camp outside Helstrom's gate; the guides there show the stair's mouth, where the deep water starts.

journal_text: The water in the Drowned Stair grows saltier the deeper I go. I'm to reach the deepest chamber, beyond one breath, and see where the salt comes in.

Deep in the Drowned Stair, a channel has been cut by hand into a brine seam, and the floods push the brine into Greenspring's roots. The cut is old. I'm to learn who made it, and Vees-Wai, the tree-minder, reads the old stakes.

Vees-Wai read me the founders' stakes. Greenspring's founders cut the channel to kill a rival grove downstream, and their deed is killing their own Hist. I'm to tell Ixo-Vaal, the root-herald, what I found and say what Greenspring should do.
At my word Ixo-Vaal will have the founders' cut sealed and the deed named at the Hist. The tree should mend, and the people of Greenspring now owe the people of the dead grove an answer.
At my word Ixo-Vaal will have the founders' cut sealed and will say nothing of who made it. The tree should mend.
At my word Ixo-Vaal will have the founders' cut reopened downstream. Greenspring's Hist is spared, and the dead grove's land will flood with brine again.

S'Tabi, the Khajiit trader on Soulrest's dock, told me that if I want quiet work I should ask for Tilts-The-Jug, who keeps the Night-Reed Chapter's desk in the house just west of him. I'm to speak to her inside that house in Soulrest.
directions: The house stands just west of S'Tabi in Soulrest.

journal_text: Tilts-The-Jug, who keeps the Night-Reed Chapter's desk, gave me three lockpicks to see how I work. Keeps-What-Floats, a thief who keeps to the shore near her door, took a sleeping Lookout's necklace of blue jaspers and keeps it in a strongbox by the houses at the water's edge. I'm to take it back without harming him; Sits-By-The-Water knows his habits.
directions: Out of the door and along the shore by the houses; Keeps-What-Floats keeps to the shore a short walk from that door.

journal_text: I talked Keeps-What-Floats round, and he gave me the key to his strongbox. I'm to open it and take the Blue Jasper Necklace, by the houses at the water's edge.
directions: The strongbox is on the bare ground by the houses at the water's edge.

journal_text: I paid Keeps-What-Floats sixty gold, and he gave me the key to his strongbox. I'm to open it and take the Blue Jasper Necklace, by the houses at the water's edge.
directions: The strongbox is on the bare ground by the houses at the water's edge.

journal_text: I took the Blue Jasper Necklace out of Keeps-What-Floats's strongbox. I'm to bring it to Tilts-The-Jug inside the house just west of S'Tabi in Soulrest.
directions: Tilts-The-Jug is inside the house just west of S'Tabi in Soulrest.

journal_text: I gave Tilts-The-Jug the Blue Jasper Necklace, and because Keeps-What-Floats came to no harm, she paid me a hundred gold. I'm to take the coast ship from Soulrest's dock to Lilmoth, go down the trapdoor on the ruin east of Lilmoth and speak to Bent-Spine.
directions: The coast ship's door is on Soulrest's dock, a fair way west of the house; inside the ship, the door at the far end of the hold comes out at Lilmoth's dock. The trapdoor is on a ruin standing in the deep water, far to the north-west of that dock. Below, Bent-Spine keeps to the inner room past the foot of the ladder.

journal_text: I gave Tilts-The-Jug the Blue Jasper Necklace, but Keeps-What-Floats is dead, and the Chapter wanted it back without a body, so she paid me nothing. I'm to take the coast ship from Soulrest's dock to Lilmoth, go down the trapdoor on the ruin east of Lilmoth and speak to Bent-Spine.
directions: The coast ship's door is on Soulrest's dock, a fair way west of the house; inside the ship, the door at the far end of the hold comes out at Lilmoth's dock. The trapdoor is on a ruin standing in the deep water, far to the north-west of that dock. Below, Bent-Spine keeps to the inner room past the foot of the ladder.

journal_text: I went down through the trapdoor east of Lilmoth to the Night-Reed Chapter under Lilmoth, and Bent-Spine, the Chapter's fence, took me in as a Lookout. Tilts-The-Jug had set me to take a stolen necklace back from Keeps-What-Floats without harming him, and what became of him is now part of how she and the Chapter think of me.
Tilts-The-Jug, who kept the Night-Reed Chapter's desk at Soulrest, is dead. The Chapter will not take me in now.
Bent-Spine, the Night-Reed Chapter's fence under Lilmoth, is dead. The Chapter will not take me in now.
Bent-Spine, the Night-Reed Chapter's fence, has work for me now that I am a Lookout. I'm to ask him about it, in the Night-Reed Chapter under Lilmoth, down the trapdoor east of Lilmoth.
directions: Bent-Spine keeps to the inner room of the Chapter, past the foot of the trapdoor's ladder.

journal_text: Bent-Spine told me a merchant drowned in the deep water south-east of the trapdoor east of Lilmoth, and his lockbox of pledges lies on the floor. He wants it emptied before its three clients find a diver, and gave me three lockpicks. I'm to dive to the lockbox, pick its lock and take what is inside.
directions: Climb the trapdoor's ladder out of the Chapter; the deep water lies south-east of the trapdoor, and the lockbox is on its floor, a short walk off, below the south bank.

journal_text: Bent-Spine gave me three more lockpicks and said there would be no others. The lockbox lies on the floor of the deep water a short walk south-east of the trapdoor east of Lilmoth, below the south bank. I'm to dive to it, pick its lock and take what is inside.
directions: Climb the trapdoor's ladder out of the Chapter; the deep water lies south-east of the trapdoor, and the lockbox is on its floor, a short walk off, below the south bank.

journal_text: In the drowned merchant's lockbox were a small bee statue, a Neesak charm in new silver and Kothringi glass beads. Neeta-Haj, Okan-Tei and Dar-Zeel each claim one, and each claim is a lie. I'm to give all three to one client, leaving the other two nothing, or sell each back the thing they lied about.
directions: The three clients are on the south bank of the deep water.

journal_text: Neeta-Haj said the bee statue was made for her clutch, but it is worn smooth, far older than any clutch of hers. I did not press her on it, and I sold it back to her for twenty gold, half its fair price. I'm to sell Okan-Tei the Newly Mounted Neesak Charm he claims, on the south bank.
directions: Okan-Tei is on the south bank of the deep water.

journal_text: Neeta-Haj said the bee statue was made for her clutch, but it is worn smooth, far older than any clutch of hers. When I said so, she bought it for forty gold, its fair price. I'm to sell Okan-Tei the Newly Mounted Neesak Charm he claims, on the south bank.
directions: Okan-Tei is on the south bank of the deep water.

journal_text: Okan-Tei said the charm was only pledged, but no one sets a pledge in a new silver mount. When I said so, he bought it for ninety gold, its fair price. I'm to sell Dar-Zeel the Kothringi Glass Beads he claims, on the south bank.
directions: Dar-Zeel is on the south bank of the deep water.

journal_text: Okan-Tei said the charm was only pledged, but no one sets a pledge in a new silver mount. I did not press him on it, and I sold it back to him for forty-five gold, half its fair price. I'm to sell Dar-Zeel the Kothringi Glass Beads he claims, on the south bank.
directions: Dar-Zeel is on the south bank of the deep water.

journal_text: I brought up the drowned merchant's statue, charm and beads from the deep water east of Lilmoth and gave all three to Neeta-Haj on the bank, who paid me a hundred and twenty gold. She gained all three, and Okan-Tei and Dar-Zeel lost theirs and will not forget who took them. The Chapter has the box off its hands.

I brought up the drowned merchant's statue, charm and beads from the deep water east of Lilmoth and gave all three to Okan-Tei on the bank, who paid me a hundred and twenty gold. He gained all three, and Neeta-Haj and Dar-Zeel lost theirs and will not forget who took them. The Chapter has the box off its hands.

I brought up the drowned merchant's statue, charm and beads from the deep water east of Lilmoth and gave all three to Dar-Zeel on the bank, who paid me a hundred and twenty gold. He gained all three, and Neeta-Haj and Okan-Tei lost theirs and will not forget who took them. The Chapter has the box off its hands.

Dar-Zeel said the beads were old family work, but they are Kothringi glass of the kind the old cairns hold. When I said so, he bought them for fifty-five gold, their fair price. Neeta-Haj, Okan-Tei and Dar-Zeel each have their own pledge again, and none was ruined. None of them thanks me for it, but I sold no one's silence.

Dar-Zeel said the beads were old family work, but they are Kothringi glass of the kind the old cairns hold. I did not press him on it, and I sold them back to him for thirty gold. Neeta-Haj, Okan-Tei and Dar-Zeel each have their own pledge again, and none was ruined. None of them thanks me for it, but I sold no one's silence.
Bent-Spine is dead. He was the Night-Reed Chapter's fence, and the job he gave me ended with him. I will not be paid for the lockbox in the deep water east of Lilmoth.
One of the drowned merchant's three clients on the bank is dead, and the pledges cannot be settled now. The job for Bent-Spine has come to nothing, and I will not be paid for it.
